input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so plain `str` filenames are no longer wrapped in a tuple.
- rationale: Trigger: `click.edit(filename="file.txt")`, which is the common documented usage. A str is not an os.PathLike, so it is passed to `edit_files` as an iterable of characters. The editor is then launched with one argument per character of the filename and opens the wrong files. The check should be `isinstance(filename, (str, os.PathLike))`.
critique: The finding names the same faulty check: it now tests only os.PathLike, so a plain str is not wrapped and is passed to edit_files as an iterable of characters. The editor then launches with one argument per character, which is exactly the labeled mechanism and failure.
